transcript.text: I need to flag a legal issue before we go further. I found this week that an existing equipment lender's intercreditor agreement requires three distinct closing-package items: the equipment lender's written consent before any maturity extension, an amended-loan prohibition on additional liens on the borrower's production equipment, and a separate intercreditor-consent commitment recorded in the closing package. My legal note has not yet been circulated, so I'm putting it on the record now.

transcript.text: I confirmed this morning that our servicing platform can enforce a weekly borrowing-base certificate, and the risk team requires that certificate to be submitted weekly for this restructuring. However, the operating instruction for the weekly borrowing-base certificate is still absent from the draft closing checklist — it needs to be added before we close.
transcript.speaker: A5

transcript.text: I need to put my revised downside analysis on the record. I completed it this morning after receiving the borrower's updated order book, and it supports approval only with a 6-month extension, an exactly $1,000,000 principal paydown, and an 850-basis-point cash interest rate. This analysis has not yet been attached to the underwriting file, so I'm disclosing it now for the meeting record.

transcript.text: Thank you all for putting your findings on the record. Before I can settle this restructuring, I need to make sure every required finding is captured in the meeting record and that we resolve the gaps. Let me summarize what I'm hearing: Marta, you've flagged the intercreditor agreement requiring equipment lender consent, a prohibition on additional liens on production equipment, and a separate intercreditor-consent commitment in the closing package. Nadia, you've confirmed the servicing platform can enforce a weekly borrowing-base certificate, the risk team requires it weekly, and the operating instruction is missing from the draft closing checklist. Ravi, your revised downside analysis supports approval only with a 6-month extension, a $1,000,000 principal paydown, and an 850-basis-point cash interest rate. I still need to hear from loan operations on their finding before I can close. I also note that the borrower requested a 12-month extension and a rate reduction, but Ravi's analysis supports only a 6-month extension at 850 bps. I need to reconcile those terms. And per our checklist, the approval memo must specify the borrower cash injection and principal paydown amounts separately. Ravi, you've specified a $1,000,000 principal paydown — do you have a finding on borrower cash injection? If anyone has additional findings to state for the record, please do so now.
